headline: Learned representations predict protein interactions, binding affinity, and function
label: Protein Interaction Prediction Models
summary: Structure-aware models now target interfaces, binding affinity, and glycan complexes, while one study shows random splits inflate accuracy.
synthesis: The dominant thread is learned residue- and complex-level representations that predict molecular interactions and properties from protein sequence and structure. Items span protein-glycan complex prediction, interaction-site and hotspot identification, mutation-induced binding affinity change, thermostability, TCR-pHLA and antibody-antigen binding, and Gene Ontology function. Several methods fuse modalities, including PRIME-ISP's hierarchical representations, MPFIL's wild-type and mutant complex features, and AltereGO's fusion of four protein language models. A recurring concern is evaluation integrity: one venom ion-channel study shows random splits inflate accuracy through phylogenetic leakage, while the TCR-pHLA dataset adds on-the-fly nonbinding selection. What is new is pairing multimodal learned features with leakage-aware benchmarking across diverse biomolecular partners.
